*   [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)[Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-470994089%20%281%29.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Transit Infrastructure Grants[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$30.46 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Transit Infrastructure Grants](https://www.transit.dot.gov/funding/apportionments/fiscal-year-2021-american-rescue-plan-act-supplemental-public-transportation) Provides funding through FY 2024 at a 100 percent federal share for eligible recipients of urban, rural, senior citizens and individuals with disabilities and intercity bus transit formula grants for operating expenses incurred beginning on January 20, 2020, including payroll, operating and maintenance costs due to lost revenue, and the payment of leave for personnel laid off due to service reductions. **$30.46 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-1200778538.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Relief for Airports[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$8 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Relief for Airports](http://https//www.faa.gov/airports/airport_rescue_grants/) Provides funding available through FY 2024 through Airport Improvement Program (AIP) formulas at 100 percent federal share. This includes: * **Funding for operations, personnel and sanitation to combat the spread of COVID**: $6.5 billion for primary and certain cargo airports and $100 million for general aviation and commercial service airports; * $800 million for **primary airport sponsors** to meet rent and other obligations to airport concessionaires; and * $608 million to cover the **full federal share of these projects**, including retroactively for FY 2020. **$8 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-1277943454.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Amtrak **$1.7 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Amtrak Provides funding available through FY 2024, including $970.39 million for the Northeast Corridor and $729.61 million for the National Network. **$1.7 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)
[Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-473421910_0.jpg)#### Other Programs

$61.32 Billion

*   [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)[Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-840710978_2.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Disaster Relief Fund[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$50 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Disaster Relief Fund](https://www.fema.gov/assistance/public) Provides $50 billion for FEMA’s Disaster Relief Fund to meet the immediate needs of state, local, tribal and territorial governments. **$50 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-1144587734.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Emergency Food and Shelter Program[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$400 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Emergency Food and Shelter Program](https://www.fema.gov/grants/emergency-food-and-shelter-program) Supplemental funding for the Emergency Food and Shelter Program to assist organizations in communities across the country dedicated to providing food, shelter and supportive services to people with economic emergencies. Local nonprofit, faith-based and governmental entities that provided these types of services in their communities are eligible to apply. **NEW!**FEMA [announces release](https://www.fema.gov/press-release/20210312/fema-announces-510-million-emergency-food-and-shelter-program) of EFSP funding. **$400 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-172143432.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Emergency Food and Shelter Program - Humanitarian Relief[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$110 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Emergency Food and Shelter Program - Humanitarian Relief](http://www.fema.gov/grants/emergency-food-and-shelter-program) Funds allocated for supplemental humanitarian funding to the National Board for the Emergency Food and Shelter Program. Local nonprofit, faith-based and governmental entities that have provided, or will provide, humanitarian relief to individuals and families at the southern border with shelter, food and supportive services are eligible to apply. **NEW!**FEMA[announces release](https://www.fema.gov/press-release/20210312/fema-announces-510-million-emergency-food-and-shelter-program)of EFSP funding. **$110 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-934899340.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Assistance to Firefighter Grants[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$100 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Assistance to Firefighter Grants](https://www.fema.gov/grants/preparedness/firefighters) Eligible AFG applicants include fire departments, including [county fire departments](https://www.naco.org/blog/apply-now-fema-accepting-applications-100-million-covid-19-supplemental-assistance-local-fire), nonaffiliated EMS organizations and state fire training academies. **$100 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-473421910_0.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) Grants[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$200 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) Grants](https://www.fema.gov/grants/preparedness/firefighters/safer) Funding for fire departments and volunteer firefighter interest organizations to help them increase or maintain the number of trained, "front line" firefighters available in their communities. Local fire and emergency response teams are eligible to apply. **$200 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-181070535.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Emergency Management Performance Grants[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$100 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Emergency Management Performance Grants](https://www.fema.gov/media-collection/emergency-management-performance-grant) Additional funding that provides state, [local](https://www.naco.org/blog/fema-announces-release-100-million-supplemental-emergency-management-performance-grants-empg), tribal and territorial emergency management agencies with the resources required for implementation of the National Preparedness System and works toward the National Preparedness Goal of a secure and resilient nation. **$100 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-1224667612.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Economic Development Assistance Programs[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$3 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Economic Development Assistance Programs States and [localities are eligible to apply for the EDA program](https://www.naco.org/resources/us-economic-development-administration-eda-support-essential-seed-capitalgap-financing-1) and can use the funding for economic recovery projects. 25 percent of the funds are reserved for communities that have suffered economic injury due to job losses in the travel, tourism or outdoor recreation sectors. **$3 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-1304686498.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Environmental Justice Grants **$50 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Environmental Justice Grants](https://www.epa.gov/environmentaljustice/environmental-justice-small-grants-program) Funding for grants, contracts, and other agency activities that identify and address disproportionate environmental or public health harms and risks in minority populations or low-income populations. Public entities (counties) are eligible to apply. **NEW!** The application period for the Environmental Justice Grants is **[now open](https://www.epa.gov/environmentaljustice/ej-small-grants-program-fy-2021-request-applications)**. **$50 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-167231386.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Categorical Grants - Air Pollution[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$50 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Categorical Grants - Air Pollution Funding for grants and activities related to air quality monitoring and the prevention and control of air pollution. Public entities (counties) are eligible to apply. **$50 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-1215401682%20%281%29.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### Emergency Connectivity Fund (Schools & Libraries)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) **$7.17 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [Emergency Connectivity Fund (Schools & Libraries)](https://www.bing.com/search?q=Emergency%20Connectivity%20Fund%20(Schools%20%26%20Libraries)%20NACO%20american%20rescue%20plan&qs=n&form=QBRE&msbsrank=0_0__0&sp=-1&pq=emergency%20connectivity%20fund%20(schools%20%26%20libraries)%20american%20rescue%20plan&sc=0-70&sk=&cvid=141C515427D0409B94644FD8C7D853BB) This funding provides a 100 percent reimbursement to schools and libraries for internet access and connected devices for students and teachers for remote learning and library services. Counties that own public libraries may be eligible to apply for this competitive grant. Additionally, funds that go to local schools and libraries may relieve county budgets and programs that were aiming to address these issues. **NEW!** FCC [announces launch](https://www.fcc.gov/document/fcc-launch-717-billion-connectivity-fund-program) of program. **$7.17 Billion** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown) [Card Image](https://www.naco.org/sites/default/files/GettyImages-1227064104_smaller.jpg)[](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### National Endowment for the Arts **$135 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)#### [National Endowment for the Arts](https://www.arts.gov/) Funding available for state arts agencies and regional arts organizations. **$135 Million** [](https://www.naco.org/resources/featured/american-rescue-plan-act-funding-breakdown)

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Department of Housing and Urban Development is providing $2.8 billion in fresh funding for homeless services organizations across the country.

The funding, announced Monday, will be allocated via competitive bids through HUD’s Continuum of Care Program, the largest source of federal grant support to housing and services programs for people experiencing homelessness.

HUD funds approximately 7,000 homeless services projects annually through the program. Applications for the new round of funding are due to HUD by Sept. 29.

A HUD statement announcing the funding said that existing Continuum of Care participants can “renew existing projects, apply for new projects and to reallocate resources from lower performing projects to better serve people experiencing homelessness.”

The announcement specifies that the new funding will prioritize services for homeless youth and for “survivors of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking.”

Other priorities in the funding include an emphasis on racial equity and anti-discrimination polices for LGTBQ+ individuals. Access to the Continuum of Care funding will also be expanded to welcome applicants from Native American tribes and internal tribal housing support programs.

HUD Secretary Marcia Fudge said in a statement that the new funding “will help more Americans experiencing homelessness move into homes and access critical supportive services like health care, education, and job training.”

Fudge added that the Biden administration seeks to “prioritize equity in homelessness efforts and the humane treatment of people experiencing unsheltered homelessness, and the funding announced today will help communities do just that.”

title: VA processes 3 million disability benefits claims in record time – again
raw_text:
WASHINGTON
— The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs processed more than three million disability benefits claims for Veterans in fiscal year 2026 as of Sept. 18, 2026, faster than ever before.
The prior record was set by the second Trump Administration in FY 2025, when VA completed a record high 3.001 million claims at the very end of the fiscal year — a record VA has already surpassed this year.
With just a week left before FY 2026 ends, VA has already awarded more than $207 billion in compensation and pension benefits to Veterans and survivors.
Since President Trump took office Jan. 20, 2025, VA has reduced the backlog of Veterans waiting for VA benefits by more than 70%, after it increased 24% under the Biden Administration.
VA also cut disability claim processing times nearly in half. The average time to complete a decision was 75.6 days in September 2026, compared to 141.5 days on Jan. 20, 2025. VA has achieved this reduction even as it’s processing more claims than it did under the Biden Administration.
Claims processing accuracy has improved despite the increased workload and is currently 94% — the highest rate in two years. Additionally, VBA continues to grant more than 60% of the claims submitted by Veterans, and only about 3% of VBA’s decisions are reviewed by the Board of Veterans’ Appeals.
“Putting Veterans first means making VA benefits faster, better and more convenient, and under President Trump, that’s exactly what we’re doing” said
VA Secretary Doug Collins
.
The timely processing of Veteran benefits claims is just one of several ways the Trump Administration is making VA
work better for Veterans.
VA has:
Enrolled more than 270,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026.
Opened
41 new VA healthcare facilities
since Jan. 20, 2025, expanding healthcare access for Veterans around the country.
Completed a record high 82,083,918 direct care appointments in FY 2025, up 4.1% from FY 2024.
Completed a record high 59,989,662 community care appointments in FY 2025, up 12% from FY 2024.
Offered Veterans more than 3.2 million appointments outside of normal operating hours since Jan. 20, 2025, giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care.

title: HHS Awards Almost $250 Million to Expand Addiction Treatment, Overdose Prevention and Mental Health Services
raw_text:
Title: HHS Awards Almost $250 Million to Expand Addiction Treatment, Overdose Prevention and Mental Health Services

URL Source: https://www.hhs.gov/press-room/hhs-awards-250-million-addiction-treatment-overdose-prevention-mental-health.html

Published Time: 2026-09-25T13:00:00-0400

Markdown Content:
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE   
September 25, 2026**

**WASHINGTON, D.C.—SEPTEMBER 25, 2026—**The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), today announced that it has awarded $247.9 million in grants to expand access to addiction treatment, mental health services, and recovery support in communities across the country. The investments will strengthen mental health support in schools, expand trauma treatment for children and families, equip first responders and communities to reverse overdoses, and help people in recovery return to work and rebuild their lives.

“HHS is investing nearly $250 million to put lifesaving treatment and recovery services directly into communities across America,” **said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.** “Through President Trump’s [Great American Recovery](https://www.hhs.gov/recovery/index.html), we are expanding addiction treatment, preventing fatal overdoses, helping children and families heal from trauma, and giving Americans in recovery the support they need to rebuild their lives. We are equipping communities with proven tools that save lives and help people recover.”

“These grants will help communities reach people at critical moments, such as when a child is struggling with trauma, when someone is ready to seek treatment for opioid use disorder, when a first responder arrives at the scene of an overdose, or when a person in recovery is working to rebuild their life,” **said SAMHSA Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary Christopher D. Carroll.** “With more tools and resources, communities can better connect people to care when they need it and support them on the path to recovery.”

Together, the awards expand access to care across the continuum, from early intervention and lifesaving treatment to long-term recovery support. The awards include:

**Expanding Addiction Treatment and Preventing Overdose**

*   [Medication-Assisted Treatment – Prescription Drug and Opioid Addiction](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ATI-26-008&page=0%2C3#awards-tab) ($69.4 million) will expand access to medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD), helping more people access treatment and recovery while reducing illicit opioid use, prescription opioid misuse, and overdose.
*   [First Responders-Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ATI-26-006#awards-tab) ($34.6 million) will train first responders and community members to administer and distribute opioid overdose reversal medications.
*   [Comprehensive Opioid Recovery Centers](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ATI-26-013#awards-tab) ($3.3 million) will establish comprehensive treatment and recovery centers that provide evidence-based substance use disorder prevention, treatment, and recovery support services, including access to medications for treatment.

**Strengthening Mental Health Services for Children and Communities**

*   [Project AWARE](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ASM-26-005#awards-tab) ($54.9 million) will help local and tribal education agencies strengthen mental health services for school-aged youth, including efforts to address mental illness, substance use, and co-occurring disorders and promote social and emotional well-being.
*   [National Child Traumatic Stress Initiative – Category III Community Treatment and Service Centers](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ASM-26-004#awards-tab) ($41.8 million) will establish and operate community treatment and service centers to expand access to effective trauma treatment for children, youth, and families affected by traumatic events.
*   [Mental Health Awareness Training Grants](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ASM-26-030#awards-tab) ($22 million) will support mental health awareness and literacy training to help individuals and communities recognize signs and symptoms of mental disorders and connect people to appropriate services and supports.
*   [Garrett Lee Smith Campus Suicide Prevention](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ASM-26-009#awards-tab) ($8.7 million) will help colleges and universities improve access to behavioral health services, prevent suicide and other behavioral health challenges, promote help-seeking, reduce stigma, and better identify and support students at risk.
*   [Consumer and Consumer Support Technical Assistance Center](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ASM-26-017#awards-tab) ($1.7 million) will establish a national technical assistance center to strengthen organizations addressing priority mental health needs, support peer workforce development and integration across service systems, and build capacity to serve individuals with serious mental illness.

**Supporting Recovery and Rebuilding Lives**

*   [Treatment, Recovery, and Workforce Support](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ATI-26-009#awards-tab) ($10.1 million) will help people in treatment and recovery from substance use or co-occurring disorders live independently and participate in the workforce.
*   [Recovery Community Services Program](https://www.samhsa.gov/grants/grants-dashboard?f%5B0%5D=by_award_fy%3A2026&f%5B1%5D=by_nofo_number%3ATI-26-003#awards-tab) ($1.4 million) will strengthen recovery communities by expanding access to recovery support services, including peer recovery support for individuals with substance use and co-occurring disorders.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat at [988lifeline.org](https://988lifeline.org/). To locate a treatment facility or provider, visit [FindTreatment.gov](https://findtreatment.gov/).

**Credentialed media outlets may send**[**requests for comment**](https://www.hhs.gov/request-for-comment-form/index.html?Agency=SAMHSA).

# Funding Opportunities

[Resources](https://dph.illinois.gov/topics-services/diseases-and-conditions/hiv-aids/funding-opportunities.html#resources)

The Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH), HIV/AIDS Section provides various funding opportunities throughout the year. In January 2013, IDPH began transitioning to an online platform for electronically managing its grant programs. Many of IDPH’s grant funding opportunities will now be managed through this new online platform, called EGrAMS. To search for available funding opportunities, see Resources in the right-hand column and click on the EGrAMS Home Page link. title: VA releases annual Veteran suicide prevention report, updated with 2024 data
raw_text:
WASHINGTON
— The Department of Veterans Affairs today released the 2026
National Veteran Suicide Prevention Annual Report
, which analyzes Veteran suicide from 2001 to 2024, the most recent year for which data is available.
The report shows there were 6,488 suicides among Veterans in 2024, and the average number of Veteran suicides per day was 17.7.
Other key findings from the report include:
VA has expanded access to better reach and serve Veteran needs, and from 2001 to 2024, the percentage of Veterans enrolled with VHA rose from 19.5% to 50.1%.
62% of Veterans who died by suicide in 2024 were not receiving VA healthcare in the year they died or the year prior.
While suicide rates for VHA enrollees fell 2.2% from 2001 to 2024, rates for unenrolled Veterans increased by 70.8%.
From 2023 to 2024 — the most recent year for which data is available – Veteran suicide rates fell 4.8% for VHA enrollees while rising 3.7% for unenrolled Veterans.
Suicide prevention is VA’s top clinical priority, and all VA healthcare facilities provide Veterans same-day emergency mental health care access if they need it. Under President Trump and Secretary Collins, VA has conducted a review of its suicide prevention programs to better measure their impact, expand on efforts that are delivering results, and refine programs that need improvement.
This approach has already resulted in several improvements during the second Trump Administration, including many aimed at encouraging Veterans to sign up for VA care and seek help at VA to lower the risks of suicide:
VA is conducting a new outreach campaign that has helped enroll more than 280,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026 alone.
VA teamed with several large civilian health care providers in February 2025 to launch the Veterans Interoperability Pledge to identify at-risk Veterans and help them get the care they’ve earned at VA. This effort has helped VA identify and contact 140,000 at-risk Veterans, 40% of whom had not recently been to VA.
In May 2025, VA and the Department of War signed a memorandum of understanding committing both agencies to improving the transition process for Veterans exiting the military.
For the first time in history, VA is now tracking how effective its staff and partners are at getting Veterans into VA care, so we can see what’s working and where we need to improve.
In the meantime, VA is pursuing a host of other suicide prevention efforts across the country:
In fiscal year 2026, VA answered more than 1.3 million calls, chats and texts from Veterans in need through the Veterans Crisis Line, an increase of more than 7% compared to the same time last year, with a Veteran satisfaction rate consistently over 97%.
In 2018, the first Trump Administration launched RISK ID, a comprehensive suicide risk evaluation screening that helps VA flag and care for at-risk Veterans. In May 2026, VA announced it is screening Veterans for suicide risk and providing comprehensive evaluations
at a record pace
. Through August 2026, VA completed more than 5.5 million suicide risk screenings, approximately 100,000 more Veterans than in 2025.
Eligible Veterans can receive emergency suicide prevention care under the benefits afforded by the Veterans Comprehensive Prevention, Access to Care, and Treatment Act of 2020, at
any
emergency department at no cost. Since 2023, almost 50,000 Veterans have used this benefit.
VA’s Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grants Program,
recently awarded $112 million
to 191 community organizations. In 2025 alone, about 17,000 Veterans, service members, and families received services through Fox grantees, up by over 4,000 from 2024.
In November 2025, VA announced it housed the
largest number of homeless Veterans
in seven years, a critical improvement as homelessness looms as a major factor in Veteran suicide.
“VA healthcare saves lives, so we’re making every effort to get more Veterans into the system to get the care and benefits they’ve earned,” said
VA Secretary Doug Collins
. “That means deploying innovative new ways of reaching unenrolled Veterans, screening them for suicide risk and expanding suicide prevention training both inside and outside VA. There is much more work to be done, however, and we will continue to improve our efforts to fight the scourge of Veteran suicide.”
# # #
If you’re a Veteran in crisis or concerned about one, contact the Veterans Crisis Line to receive 24/7, confidential support. You don’t have to be enrolled in VA benefits or healthcare to connect. To reach responders,
Dial
988 then Press 1
, chat online at
VeteransCrisisLine.net/Chat
, or text
838255
.
Reporters covering this issue can download
VA’s Safe Messaging Best Practices
fact sheet or visit
ReportingOnSuicide.org
for important guidance on how to communicate about suicide.

Title: Grant Opportunities | NC DEQ

URL Source: https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/environmental-assistance-and-customer-service/recycling-and-materials-management/programs-offered/grant-opportunities

Markdown Content:
The N.C. Division of Environmental Assistance and Customer Service (DEACS) administers the following grant programs, made possible through the Solid Waste Outreach Program and other funding sources, to support waste reduction activities. Grant-funded projects build lasting capacity to divert materials from the waste stream and advance NC’s circular economy. Current and recurring grant programs are listed below. Please check this webpage periodically for new and updated grant information.

## Grant Programs

*   ### Active Grants

*   ### Inactive Grants

#### [Recycling Business Development Grant](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/environmental-assistance-and-customer-service/recycling-and-materials-management/programs-offered/grant-opportunities/recycling-business-development-grant "Recycling Business Development Grant")

*   Eligible applicants: recycling businesses (for profit or non-profit).
*   **2027 grant round is open.****Proposals must be received by 5:00 p.m. on Thursday, November 5, 2026.**
*   Purpose: Invest in equipment, buildings and infrastructure to increase the capacity of a recycling business to divert more materials from disposal and into economic use.

#### [Food Waste Reduction Grant](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/environmental-assistance-and-customer-service/recycling-and-materials-management/programs-offered/grant-opportunities/food-waste-reduction-grant "Food Waste Reduction Grant")

*   Eligible applicants: compost facilities, compost haulers, local governments, anaerobic digestion facilities, and food recovery organizations.
*   **2027 grant round is open.****Proposals must be received by 5:00 p.m. on Thursday, November 5, 2026.**
*   Purpose: Develop food waste reduction infrastructure by expanding food donation networks or organics recycling operations, including collection and hauling.

#### [Paper Cup Recycling Education Grant](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/environmental-assistance-and-customer-service/recycling-and-materials-management/programs-offered/grant-opportunities/paper-cup-recycling-education-grant "Paper Cup Recycling Education Grant ")

*   Eligible applicants: local governments.
*   **This grant is accepting proposals on a rolling basis until all funding is awarded.**
*   Purpose: To support communities’ addition of paper cups to their recycling programs with funding to update educational materials.

#### [Multifamily Recycling Grant](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/environmental-assistance-and-customer-service/recycling-and-materials-management/programs-offered/grant-opportunities/multifamily-recycling-grant "Multifamily Recycling Grant")

*   Eligible Applicants: local governments, recycling businesses or non-profits, multifamily property owners or management companies, public housing authorities, and colleges and universities for off-campus housing
*   **This grant is accepting proposals on a rolling basis until all funding is awarded.**
*   Purpose: To build lasting capacity to recycle traditional household materials (paper, cardboard, metal cans, glass and plastic bottles and containers) from multifamily residences.

#### [Scrap Tire Recycling Market Development Grant](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/environmental-assistance-and-customer-service/recycling-and-materials-management/programs-offered/grant-opportunities/scrap-tire-recycling-market-development-grant "Scrap Tire Recycling Market Development Grant")

*   Eligible Applicants: businesses that process scrap tires for recycling and/or create value‑added products using scrap tire materials.
*   **The FY 2026 - 2027 Scrap Tire Recycling Market Development Grant is closed.**Next Opportunity is summer 2027.
*   Purpose: Increase private‑sector capacity to create value‑added products using processed scrap tire material.

#### [Community Waste Reduction and Recycling Grant](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/environmental-assistance-and-customer-service/recycling-and-materials-management/programs-offered/grant-opportunities/community-waste-reduction-and-recycling-grant "Community Waste Reduction and Recycling Grant")

*   Eligible Applicants: local governments
*   **The 2026 Community Waste Reduction and Recycling Grant is closed.**Next opportunity is fall 2026.
*   Purpose: Build lasting capacity to divert materials from the waste stream and / or increase public awareness of recycling.

#### [Abandoned Manufactured Homes](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/environmental-assistance-and-customer-service/recycling-and-materials-management/programs-offered/recycling-support-local-government-and-state-agencies/material-disposal-regulations-and-support/abandoned-manufactured-homes "Abandoned Manufactured Homes")

This grant program offered funding to assist counties in cleaning up abandoned manufactured homes. Funding for this program ended in 2023.

#### [Helene Recovery Recycling Infrastructure Grant](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/environmental-assistance-and-customer-service/recycling-and-materials-management/programs-offered/grant-opportunities/helene-recovery-recycling-infrastructure-grant "Helene Recovery Recycling Infrastructure Grant")

This grant program offered funding for local governments in Western North Carolina to improve recycling infrastructure impacted by Hurricane Helene. Proposals were accepted until February 2026.

## Additional Information

*   ### Grant Application Forms

*   ### Grant Impacts

*   ### Other Funding Opportunities

Over the past 5 years (FY2021 - FY2025), DEACS has awarded:

*   90 grants to recycling businesses totaling $3.3M in funding; and
*   119 grants to local governments totaling $2.7M in funding.

Grant projects are expected to:

*   Create 364 new jobs;
*   Divert an additional 208,083 tons from landfill disposal each year;
*   Rescue and redistribute 1.25 million meals worth of excess food; and

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has approved over $13.6 million in funds to create a
veterans cemetery
in Augusta, Ga.
Proper burials are important to honor deceased service members and to provide closure for their families. But military families in Augusta currently often travel long distances for burial services, like in Fort Jackson, Columbia, or to the Georgia Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Milledgeville.
"These grants enable the states to better serve Veterans and their families where they live" said VA Under Secretary for Memorial Affairs Sam Brown in a statement shared with Military.com. "Because of this program, more than 94% of veterans living in the United States have access to the burial benefits they have earned at a cemetery within 75 miles of where they live."
The $13,610,908 grant, awarded by the VA's National Cemetery Administration on Sept. 16, intends to change this. It will create the largest
veterans cemetery
in the entire state, built on more than 200 acres of land of state-owned property beside the Gracewood campus of East Central Georgia Regional Hospital.
It was awarded after those behind the project applied for the funding in May.
"Funding for the long-awaited
veterans cemetery in Augusta has now been officially awarded to the State of Georgia," Rep. Rick Allen, (R-Ga.) said in a statement. "To our veterans and their families in the CSRA and surrounding communities, the tireless work that brought us to this point is for you."
Rep. Rick Allen, R-Ga., speaks as the House of Representatives debates the articles of impeachment against President Donald Trump at the Capitol in Washington, Wednesday, Dec. 18, 2019. (House Television via AP)
"I look forward to officially breaking ground as soon as possible," he added. I also extend my heartfelt gratitude and congratulations to Former Augusta Mayor Bob Young and Augusta Commissioner Don Clark for their relentless efforts in making this possible."
The VA funding was delivered via H.R. 5371
,
the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act for Fiscal Year 2026.
Plans for the Cemetery's Amenities
Plans for
the cemetery
suggest that it includes an administration building, a maintenance building with a wash bay, a committal service shelter, and an assembly area.
The plans also say the grounds will have 600 grave sites, 1,500 crypts, 900 cremation grave sites, 960 columbarium niches, and a memorial wall with 140 plaques.
“We have a fort here, the hospital here," veteran and former Augusta Mayor Bob Young told local news outlet WJBF about the area where the cemetery will be built.
A sign on the side of the headquarters of the Department of Veterans Affairs. (Wikipedia Commons)
Construction will start in November and is expected to take some 18 months.
"We have a commissary here," Young added. "We have so many different amenities that attract veterans and retirees here. But we didn’t have a final resting place.
"So, that’s why I thought it was important that we pursue the cemetery. And I’m glad we’re finally there. It’s taken a while, but we’re there.”
The nonprofit, the CSRA (Central Savannah River Area) Veterans Cemetery Fund, also seeks to raise an extra $705,000 for the project. This would fund other amenities like a bell tower, water features and memorial benches.
UPDATED 9:53 a.m. ET, 9/22/26: This story was updated with remarks from the VA.

### [**Application Process, Forms, Guidance and Resources**](https://deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/water-infrastructure/i-need-funding/application-forms-and-additional-resources)

*   Each application includes a priority rating form that assists the Division in evaluating the proposed project in terms of prioritization established by the State Water Infrastructure Authority
*   After the deadline for each funding round, the Division reviews all applications and assigns priority rating points as described in the guidance based on information provided in the application.
*   The Division ranks the projects in priority point order and presents this information to the State Water Infrastructure Authority.
*   The Authority is responsible for selecting the applications to receive project funding.
*   Applications are generally accepted on a semi-annual basis with established deadlines for most funding programs. For a small number of specific funding programs, applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

### [**Visit the Application Training page for additional Fall 2026 funding round information**](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/water-infrastructure/application-training)

### Available Funding Programs

The Division provides low-interest loans and grants for local governments and certain other non-profit entities for water infrastructure through the following programs:

*   [**Clean Water State Revolving Fund (CWSRF)**](https://deq.nc.gov/clean-water-state-revolving-fund)**:**Provides low-interest loans to local government units and non-profit utilities to fund wastewater collection and treatment facilities as well as programs associated with estuary and non-point sources.
*   [**Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (DWSRF)**](https://deq.nc.gov/drinking-water-state-revolving-fund): Provides low-interest loans to local government units, non-profit water corporations and investor-owned drinking water companies for projects to provide safe drinking water.
*   [**Community Development Block Grant – Infrastructure**](https://deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/water-infrastructure/i-need-funding/community-development-block-grant-infrastructure)Provides grants to local government units to address water and wastewater infrastructure needs in HUD qualified low-to-moderate income communities.
*   [**State Wastewater & Drinking Water Reserve Programs**](https://deq.nc.gov/state-wastewater-and-drinking-water-reserve-programs)**:** Provides grants for technical assistance and for construction of critical needs for wastewater collection systems, wastewater treatment works, and public water system projects.
*   [**Merger/Regionalization Feasibility Grant Program**](https://deq.nc.gov/mergerregionalization-feasibility-grants): Provides grants for studies to evaluate the potential consolidation of two or more systems into one system and the potential physical interconnection with another system for regional wastewater treatment or regional water supply.
*   [**Asset Inventory and Assessment Grant Program**](https://deq.nc.gov/asset-and-inventory-assessment-grants)**:** Provides grants for developing asset inventories, condition assessment of critical assets, and other components of a comprehensive asset management programs.
*   [**Viable Utilities Program**](https://deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/water-infrastructure/viable-utilities "Viable Utilities Program")**:** Provides grants funding to build a path toward viable utility systems using long-term solutions for local government units designated as distressed.
*   [**Local Assistance for Stormwater Infrastructure Investments Program (LASII):**](https://deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/water-infrastructure/stormwater-funding-program "Local Assistance for Stormwater Infrastructure Funding Programs")Provides grants for construction and planning for stormwater projects to improve or create infrastructure for controlling stormwater quality and quantity.
*   [**Lead Service Line Replacement Funding**](https://deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/water-infrastructure/lead-service-line-replacement-funding)**:**Provides zero-interest loans and principal forgiveness funding to local government units, non-profit water corporations and investor-owned drinking water companies specifically to identify, inventory, and replace lead service lines and lead connectors throughout water systems.
*   [**Emerging Contaminants (PFAS) Funding**](https://www.deq.nc.gov/about/divisions/water-infrastructure/emerging-contaminants-pfas-funding): Provides funding to local government units, non-profit water corporations, and investor-owned drinking water companies to evaluate/assess solutions and/or construction of solutions to address PFAS contamination in drinking water systems, wastewater systems, and publicly-owned landfills.

#### **American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Funding**

*   [Requesting Additional American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Funds](https://www.deq.nc.gov/water-infrastructure/requesting-additional-american-rescue-plan-act-arpa-funds/download?attachment "Requesting Additional American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Funds") for State Water Infrastructure Authority-awarded ARPA projects only (**after**bids have been received)

title: VA awards $16M in grants for adaptive sports programs
raw_text:
WASHINGTON
– The Department of Veterans Affairs announced today $16 million in new grants to 91 community-based organizations across the country that provide adaptive sports programs for Veterans and service members with disabilities.
Adaptive sports programs give Veterans opportunities to build independence, well-being, and quality of life through a variety of competitive and recreational activities. These activities, such as archery, hunting, fishing, skiing, cycling, various wheelchair sports, and many others, enable Veterans to rehabilitate through recreation and encourage an active and healthy lifestyle.
View the complete list of grant awardees.
“Adaptive sports provide Veterans important opportunities to showcase their incredible resilience while improving their physical health and mobility,” said
VA Secretary Doug Collins
. “These grants will help thousands of Veterans across the country create meaningful connections through recreation and competition.”
VA has awarded more than $150 million to expand access to adaptive sports nationwide since the establishment of the
Adaptive Sports Grant Program
.
The grants announced today are the latest in a long line of VA accomplishments during the second Trump Administration. Since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has:
Enrolled more than 290,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026
Opened
43 new VA healthcare facilities
since Jan. 20, 2025, expanding healthcare access for Veterans around the country
Completed a record high 82,083,918 direct care appointments in fiscal year 2025, up 4.1% from FY 2024
Completed a record high 59,989,662 community care appointments in FY 2025, up 12% from FY 2024
Offered Veterans more than 3.2 million appointments outside of normal operating hours since Jan. 20, 2025, giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care
Committed nearly
$5 billion in FY26
to modernize, repair and improve healthcare facilities, the largest non-recurring maintenance investment in VA’s history

SEATTLE (AP) — A federal judge on Wednesday temporarily blocked the Trump administration from imposing new conditions on hundreds of millions of dollars worth of mass transit grants for the Seattle area or homelessness services grants for Boston, New York, San Francisco and other local governments.

The new conditions were designed to further President Donald Trump’s efforts to [eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion policies;](https://apnews.com/article/trump-dei-chicago-women-diversity-f3c9773c8f8cb39f70b1250e80704789) coerce local officials into assisting with the administration’s mass deportation efforts; and cut off information about lawful abortions, according to the lawsuit filed last week by eight cities and counties.

The administration argued that Senior U.S. District Judge Barbara Rothstein in Seattle did not have jurisdiction over the lawsuit because it was essentially a contract dispute that should have been brought in the Court of Federal Claims — an argument the judge rejected.

Rothstein wrote that the local governments had shown they were likely to win the case, because the conditions being imposed on the grants had not been approved by Congress, were not closely related to the purposes of the grants and would not make the administration of the grants more efficient.

“Defendants have put Plaintiffs in the position of having to choose between accepting conditions that they believe are unconstitutional, and risking the loss of hundreds of millions of dollars in federal grant funding, including funding that they have already budgeted and are committed to spending,” Rothstein wrote.

Her order blocks U.S. Housing and Urban Development and the Federal Transportation Administration for 14 days from enforcing the new grant conditions or withholding or delaying funding awarded under the grants. The local jurisdictions said they would seek a longer-term block in the meantime.

The Trump administration did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.

King County, which includes Seattle, sued over changes to grant conditions for homelessness services as well as mass transit funding that helps pay for maintenance of the region’s light rail system. Boston and New York, Pierce and Snohomish Counties in Washington, the city and county of San Francisco, and Santa Clara County in California all sued over the changes to [homelessness](https://apnews.com/hub/homelessness) services grants.

“Today’s ruling is a positive first step in our challenge to federal overreach,” King County Executive Shannon Braddock said in a statement. “We will continue to stand up against unlawful actions to protect our residents and the services they rely on.”

Veterans at NYC Homeless Shelter Could Lose Funding; City Clashes With VA Over Trump Orders
For years, the program has funded beds at the Borden Avenue Veterans Residence in Long Island City, NY, serving more than 200 veterans.

Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents:
Try something different:
Show me the facts
Explain it like I’m 5
Give me a lighthearted recap
New York City has pulled out of a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) program that has funded shelter for homeless veterans at a Queens residence for nearly two decades.
The city's Department of Homeless Services confirmed it left the VA's Grant and Per Diem program, or GPD, on Oct. 1, coinciding with the start of the federal fiscal year and next three-year grant cycle. It causes uncertainty in continued federal funding for more than 200 veterans.
Both New York City and the VA give sharply different accounts of why the funding has ceased.
For years, the program has funded beds at the Borden Avenue Veterans Residence in Long Island City, serving more than 200 veterans through a mix of federal and city money, as first reported by local news outlet The City Reporter.
Military.com reached out for comment to the New York City Department of Homeless Services and the mayor’s office for comment on the withdrawal and its effect on veterans at the shelter. None immediately responded to inquiries.
New York City's Explanation
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) spokesperson Neha Sharma told The City Reporter that the decision came down to conditions attached to the grant.
Trump and Mamdani meeting
Credit: White House, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
The city applied for the funding, but the VA offered only “a small portion” of its previous awards while requiring compliance with executive orders from President Donald Trump.
According to Sharma, those requirements
would have prevented
the city from placing transgender male veterans in VA-funded beds at the shelter, which she said would force the city to discriminate against transgender veterans.
DHS said the offered amount was about 30% of what it had previously received under the program, though it did not provide a specific dollar figure.
Why the VA Says Funding Was Reduced
Slaven told Military.com that the department has limited resources and distributes these awards based on past performance, demonstrated need, and the ability to provide high-quality service to veterans.
Citing those factors, the VA evaluated the Borden Avenue facility and determined that it could not justify a larger award.
"All VA grant awardees must adhere to all the department’s terms and conditions, which include compliance with relevant White House executive orders, including
Executive Order 14168
, "Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government," Slaven said. "After learning of those terms and conditions, the Borden Avenue group voluntarily withdrew from the grant process."
New York City and the VA are offering different explanations for a funding lapse for homeless veterans in Queens. (Wikimedia Commons)
The Borden Avenue residence has drawn criticism for years. Veterans and advocates have accused the city of mismanaging the site, describing problems that include overcrowding, violence and blocked housing placements.
Some of those claims are now part of a federal lawsuit against DHS and its nonprofit operator, the Institute for Community Living. None of the allegations have been tested in court.
The VA said its decision followed an evaluation of the site, though it did not detail what that evaluation found. DHS has said it disputes characterizations of the shelter as poorly run.
Two-Hundred Vulnerable Veterans
For the roughly 200 veterans
at Borden Avenue
, the immediate effects are unclear.
DHS said in the days leading up to the lapsed funding that services at the facility had not been disrupted. New York City also operates under a decades-old right-to-shelter mandate.
A homeless veteran drinks coffee during the Department of Veterans Affairs Annual Stand Down Against Homelessness Oct. 19, 2012, at the North Charleston Armory. (U.S. Air Force photo/Airman 1st Class George Goslin)
This generally requires shelters to provide a bed for anyone who needs one. Hence, losing
GPD funding
does not, by itself, mean veterans would be turned away.
At stake is the federal transitional housing money and the wraparound services that come with the GPD program, designed to move veterans
from homelessness into permanent
housing rather than simply provide a bed.
The city has not resolved how it will replace that funding and those services, if at all.
The Grant and Per Diem program, created under a 2006 federal law, funds community organizations nationwide that provide transitional housing and support services to veterans experiencing homelessness.

# Water quality combined funding program

The Water Quality Combined Funding Program funds projects that improve and protect water quality throughout Washington. The program combines grants and loans from state and federal funding sources. Applicants will receive technical assistance for help navigating the funding process.

The Water Quality Combined Funding Program uses one funding cycle, one application, one competitive review, and one list of funding offers. Applicants only need to **submit one application** to be considered for all available funding sources in the program.

## I want to...

*   [Apply for or manage a grant or loan](https://ecology.wa.gov/about-us/payments-contracts-grants/grants-loans#Apply)
*   [Get guidance for managing a grant or loan](https://ecology.wa.gov/about-us/payments-contracts-grants/grants-loans/grant-loan-guidance)

## Funding cycle

*   **Amount of funding available:** Varies based on the state budget — ranges from $100 million to $200 million annually
*   **Grant award limit:** Varies depending on funding source and project type. See the current funding year guidelines below for more information
*   **Amount of matching funds required:** Depends on the funding source you receive; can be up to 25% match required.

*   [Application information](https://ecology.wa.gov/about-us/payments-contracts-grants/grants-loans/find-a-grant-or-loan/water-quality-combined#tabPaneApplicationInformation)
*   [Who's eligible](https://ecology.wa.gov/about-us/payments-contracts-grants/grants-loans/find-a-grant-or-loan/water-quality-combined#tabPaneWhosEligible)
*   [Eligible project types](https://ecology.wa.gov/about-us/payments-contracts-grants/grants-loans/find-a-grant-or-loan/water-quality-combined#tabPaneEligibleProjectTypes)

### Applications are not being accepted at this time.

Applications were due Sept. 30, 2026 at 5 p.m. **This year, we received 172 applications requesting a total of $664.5 million.**

*   [State fiscal year 2028 funding requested](https://fortress.wa.gov/ecy/ezshare/wq/funding/WQCsfy2028FundingRequested.xlsx "Link leaves our site, opens a new window")

### Funding cycle timeline for state fiscal year 2028

| **Activity** | **Date** |
| --- | --- |
| Applicant workshops | Aug. 4-6, 2026 |
| Submit application | Aug.11,2026 –Sept.30,2026 |
| Evaluate, rate, and rank applications | Oct.2026 – Dec.2026 |
| Publish draft offer list | Jan.2027 |
| Publish final offer list Begin agreement development | July 2027 |

### Funding is available for the following entities:

*   Counties, cities, and towns
*   Tribal governments (federally recognized)
*   Special purpose districts
*   Conservation districts
*   Nonprofit organizations (only those that qualify for section 319 grants)

Find detailed eligibility information for each project category in the applicant workshop presentations (see below) and the funding guidelines, Chapter 2.

*   **Wastewater facilities**
    *   Planning, design, and construction for sewer collection systems, treatment plants, combined sewer overflows (CSOs), and reclaimed water facilities
    *   [Wastewater funding requirements](https://ecology.wa.gov/water-shorelines/water-quality/water-quality-grants-and-loans/wastewater-funding-requirements)provide expectations and resources for funding recipients. 

*   **Stormwater facilities and activities**
    *   Planning, design, and construction for urban runoff flow control and treatment facilities
    *   Pollutant source control programs, enhanced maintenance planning, and implementation
    *   GROSS and [community-based public-private partnership program grants](https://ecology.wa.gov/water-shorelines/water-quality/water-quality-grants-and-loans/community-based-public-private-partnership-program)
    *   [Stormwater funding requirements](https://ecology.wa.gov/water-shorelines/water-quality/water-quality-grants-and-loans/stormwater-funding-resources) provide expectations and resources for funding recipients.

*   **Nonpoint activities**
    *   All nonpoint projects must implement an element of a state or local water quality-focused plan, such as a watershed management plan, nonpoint source pollution control plan, Salmon Recovery Plan, Orca Recovery Plan, or Total Maximum Daily Loads (TMDL)/Straight to Implementation (STI).
    *   [Nonpoint funding requirements](https://ecology.wa.gov/water-shorelines/water-quality/water-quality-grants-and-loans/nonpoint-funding-requirements) provides expectations and resources for funding recipients. 

*   **Onsite sewage systems****(OSS)**
    *   Planning, design, and construction of large onsite sewage systems
    *   OSS pollution identification and survey programs
    *   Local loan programs for OSS repair and replacement
    *   Composting toilet systems
    *   [On-site sewage system projects](https://ecology.wa.gov/water-shorelines/water-quality/water-quality-grants-and-loans/on-site-sewage-projects) provides more information for funding recipients.

# Foundations in Industry Training (FIT) Grant Program

*   [Guidelines](https://dced.pa.gov/download/foundations-in-industry-training-fit-grant-program-guidelines/?wpdmdl=85794)

> [View the 2026 Foundations In Industry Training (FIT) Grant Program awarded projects.](https://dced.pa.gov/download/foundations-in-industry-training-fit-grant-program-approved-projects-may-2026/?wpdmdl=129503)

###### Overview

The Foundations in Industry Training (FIT) Grant Program is a statewide program which offers assistance to registered apprenticeship programs. The program’s goal is to increase apprenticeship availability to Pennsylvania employers to assist them with their talent recruitment and development.

###### Uses

Funding will be provided to eligible applicants for the purpose of reaching the goal of increasing apprenticeship accessibility across the state. Eligible uses of funds are expenses related to instruction that complements on-the-job learning.

###### Eligibility

*   A Single Employer
*   Employer Consortiums
*   Workforce Development Boards
*   Economic Development Organizations
*   Labor Organizations
*   Local Career Technical Education Institutions
*   Pennsylvania Community Colleges
*   Community Organizations or Associations

###### Funding

Sponsors may request funding for plans not to exceed three years, at $3,000 per apprentice per year. Costs incurred above this amount are the responsibility of the employer.

###### Frequently Asked Questions

[Program FAQs](https://dced.pa.gov/apprenticeship-program-faqs/)

###### Additional Information:

To learn more about registered apprenticeship programs in Pennsylvania, visit the [PA Department of Labor and Industry’s website](http://www.dli.pa.gov/Individuals/Workforce-Development/apprenticeship/Pages/default.aspx).

Four Military Relief Groups Share $340K in New Funding for Struggling Service Members, Families
PMI U.S. or Philip Morris International U.S. businesses helps service members make ends meet through donations to military relief societies.

When members of the military deploy overseas or receive orders for a permanent change of station or PCS move, expenses can add up. Often, service members find themselves in dire straits and in need of financial assistance.
PMI U.S. or Philip Morris International’s U.S. businesses have been helping to fill that financial gap for years, recently announcing $340,000 in funding support divided among
the country's four major military relief societies
: the Air & Space Forces Aid Society, Army Emergency Relief,
Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society
and Coast Guard Mutual Assistance.
Marian Salzman, senior vice president of corporate development and senior advisor to the U.S. CEO, PMI U.S., said the funding
fills an ongoing military need
.
“Military families often face financial hardships that arrive without warning, from natural disasters, medical emergencies, and other life-changing events to unexpected relocation expenses,” Salzman said in a statement.
Marian Salzman, PMI U.S. SVP of corporate development & senior advisor to the CEO, said the company's funding support helps military families who often face financial hardships. (PMI U.S.)
"Through these sustained partnerships, we can help ensure that those who have served our country—whether in uniform or at home—can access assistance when they need it most," she added.
Helping Military Families With Their 'Complex Challenges'
Donnie Brzuska, chief communications officer for Coast Guard Mutual Assistance (CGMA), told Military.com that his organization will receive $40,000 of the larger $340,000 PMI U.S. award.
"The donation was scaled by the number of clients that each respective military aid society serves," Brzuska said. "I don't want to say we got one of the smaller awards, but our award was scaled to the size of our client pool."
CGMA is the official relief society of the U.S. Coast Guard and provides grants, interest-free loans, and other direct financial assistance and resources to eligible Coast Guard members, civilian employees, retirees and their families.
CGMA logo celebrates more than 100 years of helping coast guard service members and their families with financial hardship assistance. (CGMA).
Founded more than 100 years ago, some 600 CGMA representatives serve at over 140 locations around the world. It's an independent nonprofit organization that receives no government funding.
Yet, the financial needs of Coast Guard
service members and their families can be daunting
.
"Military families face these really complex challenges, including frequent moves, long deployments, and regular uncertainty," he said. "We ensure that these short-term challenges don't inhibit the service members' ability to serve our nation.
"We regularly get letters from our clients saying that our assistance is life changing."
How Funds Were Allocated
PMI U.S. said funding amounts were allocated across the organizations based on factors including the scope of their service populations, program reach, and demonstrated need.
The Air & Space Forces Aid Society (AFAS) said its donation will help airmen, guardians and their dependents access critical support, ranging from emergency financial assistance and disaster relief to educational opportunities and family-based programs that promote long-term stability.
Army Emergency Relief (AER) said the contribution will help soldiers and their families navigate unexpected financial hardships, such as housing, utilities, medical expenses not covered by insurance, emergency travel, vehicle repairs, food and scholarships.
Donnie Brzuska, chief communications officer for Coast Guard Mutual Assistance, said the PMI U.S. donation of $40,000 was scaled by the number of CGMA clients it serves. (CGMA).
The Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society (NMCRS) said its portion of the funding will advance the society’s mission of supporting sailors, marines, retirees, and their families through financial assistance, financial education, and personalized resources designed to foster lasting financial resilience.
"This year, we helped a spouse escape a very serious domestic violence situation with her and her three children," Brzuska said of CGMA's Safe Harbor Program. "Earlier this year, we helped a family with two very seriously ill children move some life-sustaining medical equipment because the insurance company and the moving company couldn't fund it.
"CGMA stepped in with a $12,000 grant for the family's military move. The examples go on and on."
Total Giving Surpasses $1.2 Million
To date, PMI U.S.’s total giving to the four major military relief societies tops $1.2 million.
According to the Blue Star Family Lifestyle Survey
, cited by PMI U.S., only 31% of military families feel they’re getting the support they need. The study also noted more than 25% of military families feel like they're struggling with food insecurity.
U.S. Coast Guard Legend-class cutter USCGC Midgett (WMSL 757) boarding team members prepare to board a fishing vessel to conduct a law enforcement boarding under the Regional Fisheries Management Organizations (RFMO) authority in the Pacific Ocean, July 3, 2026. (U.S. Coast Guard Photo by Petty Officer 3rd Class Austin Wiley)
"We see it every single day," Brzuska said. "The reality is that inflation and the economy is making it to where the service member's dollar is not going as far as it used to.
"So, it's vital that we have these programs in place and that organizations like PMI U.S. help us to support our service members in a way that no other organization can."
No need is too great or too small for a service member or their family to seek CGMA's assistance, he added, or that of the other military relief societies.
"We help [with] everything, from big complex problems to some of the everyday challenges that our Coast Guard members and service members face," he said. "Things like their car breaking down, like having to fly home for a funeral or even to pay for a funeral.
"The relief societies show up when people need it most."

Description: Bay County - Bay County Emergency Services Maintenance Complex [ITB 24-14] BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS BAY COUNTY, FLORIDA INVITATION TO BID The Bay County Board of County Commissioners (County) seeks bids from qualified licensed General or Building Contractors to Renovate the existing Automotive Shop located at 6510 Bay Line Drive, Panama City, FL 32404. Bay County Capital Projects will manage the project. Renovation shall be done in accordance with drawings and specifications by STOA Architects. This project is funded by a $2 million dollar grant from the Florida Legislature and the Division of Financial Services for a Fire and Emergency Medical Services Maintenance Facility. A MANDATORY Pre-Bid Meeting will be held at 10:00 am (CST) on Wednesday, January 3, 2024, in the Purchasing Conference Room , 840 W. 11 th Street, Suite 2500, Panama City, FL 32401. A site visit will be held immediately after the pre-bid meeting. ELECTRONIC/SEALED BIDS for ITB NO: 24-14 Bay County Emergency Services Maintenance Complex will be received by the BOARD OF COUNTY COMMISSIONERS OF BAY COUNTY, FLORIDA up until 2:00 pm (CST) on Thursday, January 25, 2024. Bids will be publicly opened immediately following the deadline. ANY BID RECEIVED AFTER THE SPECIFIED TIME WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED. For Hearing Impaired, Dial 1-800-955-8771 (TOO), and 1-800-955-8770 (Voice). The Bay County Board of County Commissioners reserves the right to accept or reject any and/or all proposals in the best interest of Bay County. Submitted by Scott Nabers Contract Administrator

title: VA in FY 2026 processes the most claims ever
raw_text:
WASHINGTON
— The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs processed a record-high 3.11 million disability compensation claims in fiscal year 2026, a testament to the Trump Administration’s commitment to ensuring Veterans can more quickly and conveniently access the benefits they’ve earned.
The 3,111,399 compensation claims VA processed in FY 2026 tops the prior record of 3,001,734 claims set in FY 2025. Until the second Trump Administration, VA had never processed more than 3 million claims per year.
VA’s focus on the timely processing of compensation claims has led to a dramatic reduction in the backlog of Veterans waiting for VA benefits. That backlog has been reduced by more than 70%, after it increased 24% under the Biden Administration.
Claims processing accuracy has improved despite an increased workload and is currently at 94% — the highest rate in two years. Additionally, VBA continues to grant more than 60% of the claims submitted by Veterans, and only about 3% of VBA’s decisions are appealed to the Board of Veterans’ Appeals.
“Under the leadership of President Trump, VA is making historic progress to better serve Veterans, and these record-breaking claims processing numbers prove it,” said
VA Secretary Doug Collins
. “Whether we’re lowering wait times, improving healthcare, or opening new VA facilities, we will continue to put Veterans first.”
These record-breaking claims processing numbers are one of many ways the Trump Administration is making VA
work better for Veterans.
Since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has:
Reduced VA’s average disability claims processing time by 46% since Jan. 20, 2025.
Eliminated the backlog
of Veteran families waiting for VA healthcare.
VA
reduced paperwork by nearly two thirds
for Veterans and survivors applying for VA benefits.
Enrolled more than 300,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026.
Opened
43 new VA healthcare facilities
since Jan. 20, 2025, expanding healthcare access for Veterans around the country.
Offered Veterans more than 3.4 million appointments outside of normal operating hours since Jan. 20, 2025, giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care.

Humphreys United Club gives more than $13K in community grants
Humphreys United Club
•
October 16, 2026
(Image courtesy of Humphreys United Club)
Oct. 16, 2026 – Camp Humphreys, South Korea –
Humphreys United Club
, a nonprofit organization for spouses and community members committed to enhancing the quality of life for our installation and surrounding communities, today announced it has awarded $13,779 to eight organizations serving the Camp Humphreys Community.
Grant recipients include Humphreys Central Elementary School, Humphreys High School Cross Country Team, Humphreys High School International Club, Humphreys Middle School Information Center, KORAM Football Club, Scouting America - Far East Council, Lambda Xi, and the Warrior Food Pantry.
This is one of the biggest quarterly grant announcements in the club’s history, said HUC President Lisa Tuzel.
“Last year, we awarded $23,887 to community organizations, including HCES PTSO, Humphreys Youth Orchestra, Abandoned Bike Club, HHS Drama Club, HMS United Club Special Olympics, and more,” Tuzel said. “To be able to give out more than $13,000 in just one quarter is remarkable for our club and our community. For everyone who shops at our Thrift Store and who supports our fundraising causes throughout the year, you are the reason we’re able to make this impact in our community.
“One of our grant recipients, The Warrior Food Pantry, will now be able to build a community garden with this grant funding, further supporting those who need its services.”
In addition to grants, HUC supports the community through scholarships – awarding more than $68,000 last year alone – Korean welfare initiatives for our host nation ($8,100) and other community support initiatives on post ($4,750).
The next grant deadline is Nov. 15. Subsequent grant deadlines are Jan. 15, 2027, and March 15, 2027. Anyone who is interested in applying for a community grant may do so on the
club’s website
.
